title: Field-wise golden-sample diff adapter for structured-output regressions
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Summary:
We need a lightweight adapter that computes field-level regression signals by diffing current model/config outputs against a curated set of golden examples. The adapter will produce per-field and per-example scores (preservation, type-consistency, value-drift) and aggregate them into time-series metrics that can be used by rollouts, canaries, and alerting rules.

Goals:
- Detect targeted regressions against structured outputs (JSON) that are missed by token-level metrics.
- Provide explainable field-level signals so PMs/Eng can see which schema fields regressed after a model or config change.
- Integrate into existing canary and rollout pipelines so automatic gates can fail fast.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not replace full end-to-end evals or human review; it's an automated early-warning signal. It also does not implement remediation policies (that's a follow-up).

Design notes and approach:
1) Golden corpus: curated ~2k examples across critical routes (chat, structured forms, extraction). Examples are tagged by route, expected schema, and acceptance tolerance.
2) Field anchoring: for each golden example, the adapter matches fields by JSONPath and expected schema. For each field compute:
   - Type match (boolean): preserved expected JSON type
   - Structural match (boolean): array lengths, optional fields present/absent
   - Value similarity (continuous): normalized edit distance or semantic similarity for free-text fields (using embedding cosine if field is longer than 20 chars).
   - Enumeration drift: for enum fields compute frequency shift vs baseline.
3) Aggregation: produce per-field time-series: fail_rate, avg_similarity, p50/p95 similarity, and a sensitivity-weighted regression score. Produce route-level rollup and global health index.
4) Triggering and thresholds: configurable thresholds per-field and per-route. Default conservative thresholds derived from historical variability over last 30 days.
5) Storage & metrics: push lightweight summaries to our observability pipeline as metrics (prometheus-style labels: project/route/model/config_sha/field). Persist per-example diffs in blob store (S3) for inspection when alerts fire.
6) Integration points:
   - Canary runner: evaluate new model/config on golden corpus and fail canary if field regression score > threshold.
   - Console: new Output Integrity dashboard with top regressed fields, exemplar diffs, and trend lines.

Trade-offs considered:
- Per-example vs sampling: full corpus gives stronger signals but costs more; we will start with a 2k golden set and implement sampled refreshes.
- Similarity metric: edit-distance is cheap but brittle for paraphrases; embeddings are robust but more compute. We will hybridize: short fields use edit-distance, long/textual fields use embedding-based cosine.
- Storage: storing all per-field token diffs is too heavy; we store summarized diffs and only persist full diffs for examples that triggered alerts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Adapter runs as a job in canary pipeline and emits per-field metrics for a given model/config SHA.
2) Console dashboard receives and displays top-10 regressed fields with at least one exemplar diff link.
3) Canary blocks when configured threshold exceeded and an automated message with summary + link to diffs is created in rollout run.
4) Unit tests covering type-match, structural-match, value-similarity heuristics and end-to-end smoke on a small golden set.
